commit a0582df921fd1c89d60dfaaea36ed90abd619f8f
Author: lazizbekravshanov <lazizravshanov1998@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Apr 15 16:42:39 2026 -0400

    docs(pt-br): update Portuguese GUI tutorials to say "main" instead of "master"
    
    The English versions of these GUI tutorials were updated to refer to
    the `main` branch (the project's actual default branch). The
    Brazilian Portuguese translations still said `branch master` /
    `rama master`, and several files contained backlink URLs pointing at
    `/blob/master/translations/README.pt_br.md` — both branch-name- and
    path-stale (the file lives at `docs/translations/README.pt_br.md`
    now, no longer at the repo root).
    
    Files updated (each touched in both the flat `translations/` location
    and the duplicate `translations/Portuguese/` location):
    
    - gitkraken-tutorial.pt-br.md (2 lines: push-target + closing note)
    - github-windows-vs-code-tutorial.pt_br.md (1 line: closing note)
    - github-windows-vs-code-tutorial_pt_br.md (2 lines: closing note +
      backlink URL)
    - github-windows-vs2017-tutorial.pt_br.md (1 line: backlink URL)
    - github-windows-intellij-tutorial.pt_br.md (2 lines: closing note +
      backlink URL)
    
    10 files touched in total — 5 distinct translations, each in two
    locations. Both copies are reachable from links in the repo, so

commit f1814aafc0f5028684b2b55681300b0152ca942f
Author: lazizbekravshanov <lazizravshanov1998@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Apr 14 13:00:18 2026 -0400

    docs(uz): fix broken relative links in README.uz.md and sync git-switch fallback
    
    Issues in the Uzbek translation that made the page partially broken:
    
    - The links to "Additional material" and the GUI-tool-tutorials table
      used `additional-material/...` and `gui-tool-tutorials/...` as if the
      file were at the repo root, but README.uz.md lives at
      docs/translations/, so every one of those links resolved to
      docs/translations/additional-material/... (a path that doesn't
      exist). Other translations (Spanish, Korean) correctly prefix `../`,
      and this is what the Uzbek file now does too.
    - The "if git doesn't exist, install it" link pointed at
      help.github.com/articles/set-up-git/ — the English README was
      updated to docs.github.com/en/get-started/quickstart/set-up-git;
      the Uzbek link is now synced to the same canonical URL.

commit b87654221d0277b71795d3f588dce92d6d14adbf
Author: lazizbekravshanov <lazizravshanov1998@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Apr 14 12:54:17 2026 -0400

    docs: replace stale "master" branch references with "main"
    
    The repository's default branch is main (see recent commits on origin/main),
    but several tutorials still told readers their PRs would be merged into
    "master" or described the default branch of this repo as master. That's
    factually wrong today and confuses first-time contributors checking their
    fork against the GitHub UI.
    
    Updated files:
    - gui-tool-tutorials/github-desktop-tutorial.md
    - gui-tool-tutorials/github-desktop-old-version-tutorial.md
    - gui-tool-tutorials/gitkraken-tutorial.md
    - gui-tool-tutorials/sublime-merge-tutorial.md
    - gui-tool-tutorials/sourcetree-macos-tutorial.md
    - gui-tool-tutorials/github-windows-intellij-tutorial.md
    - gui-tool-tutorials/github-windows-vs-code-tutorial.md
    - gui-tool-tutorials/github-windows-vs2017-tutorial.md (including a
      screenshot caption for the "Branch: master" dropdown that no longer
      matches the current GitHub UI)
    - additional-material/git_workflow_scenarios/removing-branch-from-your-repository.md
    - additional-material/git_workflow_scenarios/moving-a-commit-to-a-different-branch.md
      (comment that referred to "move master back" — the scenario is branch-agnostic)
    - additional-material/git_workflow_scenarios/removing-a-file.md
      (example used `git push origin master`; now reads `git push origin main`
      with a note that the user should substitute their branch)
    
    Translations under docs/translations/ and docs/gui-tool-tutorials/translations/
    still reference master and should be updated by the respective language
    reviewers (per .github/CONTRIBUTING.md). Documented in audit notes.
    
    Git-flow methodology references (gitflow.md) are intentionally left as
    "master" because the Git Flow model canonically uses that name.

Author: jesuslln <57109517+jesuslln@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sat Feb 22 12:48:02 2025 +0000

    Spanish flag name (#94665)
    
    Spanish flag name is a bit weird. 'Española' is an adjetive to refer to
    something that is spanish like the language or the flag.
    Instead 'Español' is the sustantive to refer to the languague,
    just like they have use for other countries in the project.
    
    I added the whole 'Español de España' to be consistent with the
    flags from México and Ecuador. I am sure more latin contributors
    will come soon and they will add more flags to the project.
